issues.detail: The Hebrew 'לֹא כְתוֹרָתֶךָ' means 'not according to Your law' (referring to God's law, i.e., the psalmist's own law/instruction from God). The Vietnamese renders it as 'việc không theo luật pháp của Đức Giê-hô-va' ('things not according to the law of Jehovah'), which adds 'việc' (things) and changes the possessive from 'Your' (second person, addressing God) to 'của Đức Giê-hô-va' (of Jehovah, third person). This shifts the perspective and adds a noun not present in the Hebrew, altering the meaning slightly.
